name: Number of solutions 0<k<n to the equation sigma(n) = sigma(k) + sigma(n-k), where sigma is the sum of divisors function.
comment: The number of solutions is always even because k=n/2 cannot be a solution for even n.
link: Antti Karttunen, Table of n, a(n) for n = 1..16384
Eric Li, A resolution of Erdős Problem 1061 on the sum-of-divisors function, arXiv preprint (2026), arXiv:2606.25849 [math.NT].
mathematica: a[n_] := Select[Range[n-1], DivisorSigma[1, n]==DivisorSigma[1, n-# ]+DivisorSigma[1, # ]&]; Table[Length[a[n]], {n, 150}]
xref: Cf. A110176 (least k such that sigma(n)=sigma(k)+sigma(n-k)).
author: _T. D. Noe_, Jul 15 2005
